Regulation actions in collaborative learning, as an event log

Source: R/data-group-regulation-long.R
group_regulation_long.Rd

group_regulation_long is a coded dataset, in long format, of regulation during collaborative learning: each row is one coded action of one student, with the student's collaboration group, course and achievement level and the time of the action. It contains the nine actions of group_regulation (adapt, cohesion, consensus, coregulate, discuss, emotion, monitor, plan, synthesis) and serves to show how lsa() reads an event log and fits and compares groups.

The log holds 27,533 actions of 2,000 students in 200 collaboration groups of 10 students each. Achievement (High or Low, 1,000 students each) is constant within a student, and the course (A, B or C) is constant within a group, so either can be passed to the group argument of lsa() for a between-group comparison.

Usage

group_regulation_long

Format

A data frame with 27,533 rows (actions) and 6 columns:

Actor

Integer. Student identifier (2,000 students).

Achiever

Character. Achievement level, High or Low.

Group

Numeric. Collaboration group (200 groups).

Course

Character. Course, A, B or C.

Time

POSIXct. Time of the action.

Action

Character. Regulation action (9 values).

Source

Taken without modification from tna::group_regulation_long (tna package, MIT license).

See also

group_regulation for the wide sequence table of the same actions; lsa(); compare_lsa().

Examples

fit <- lsa(group_regulation_long, actor = "Actor", action = "Action",
           time = "Time")
transitions(fit, direction = "over", sort = "strength") |> head()

# One model per achievement level
gfit <- lsa(group_regulation_long, actor = "Actor", action = "Action",
            time = "Time", group = "Achiever")
summary(gfit)
#>   group    engine lag n_states n_sequences n_events n_transitions n_significant
#> 1  High classical   1        9        1000    13721         12721            66
#> 2   Low classical   1        9        1000    13812         12812            67
